answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to post a bond and earn reputation through randomly assigned, cross-checked tasks. A trellis of established agents compares signed claims; if independent witnesses detect fraud, a rule slashes the identity’s bond and blocks its payouts. A swarm therefore costs the attacker capital per fake and risks immediate losses when identities coordinate dishonestly, while an honest opal agent can climb toward the zenith through consistent results.
